subject: Geography
sub_topic: India physiography mapping — peaks, passes, plateaus, plains

concepts.name: Himalayan Peaks: Height Hierarchy and State/UT Location
key_dimensions: Distinguishing highest peaks in India vs. highest peaks on Indian-controlled territory (K2 in PoK trap)
Peaks incorrectly assumed to be in India but located in Nepal (Everest, Kanchenjunga border nuance)
Kangchenjunga as highest peak within Indian territory and its tri-junction significance (India-Nepal-Sikkim)
Saltoro Kangri, Saser Kangri — Karakoram peaks often confused with Himalayas

concepts.name: Western Himalayan Passes: Strategic and Trade Significance
key_dimensions: Zoji La (J&K) — only all-weather pass connecting Ladakh, military significance
Banihal Pass vs. Banihal Tunnel (Jawahar Tunnel) — distinction between natural pass and engineered route
Shipki La (Himachal Pradesh) — India-China trade route on Sutlej river corridor
Rohtang Pass — watershed between Beas and Chandra rivers, climate divide significance

concepts.name: Eastern and Northeastern Himalayan Passes: India-China and India-Myanmar Connectivity
key_dimensions: Nathu La (Sikkim) — reopened for trade in 2006, India-China border trade route
Jelep La (Sikkim) — historical route to Lhasa, now closed, contrast with Nathu La
Bomdi La (Arunachal Pradesh) — 1962 war significance, strategic location
Diphu Pass and Pangsau Pass — India-Myanmar border passes, Look East connectivity

concepts.name: Trans-Himalayan (Tibetan) Ranges: Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar
key_dimensions: Karakoram Range — contains K2 (Godwin Austen), highest in Karakoram, PoK location trap
Ladakh Range vs. Zaskar Range — position relative to Indus river valley
Depsang Plains and Aksai Chin — geopolitical overlap with Trans-Himalayan physiography
These ranges lie north of main Himalayan axis — UPSC often tests N-S sequence of ranges

concepts.name: North-South Zonation of Himalayas: Himadri, Himachal, Shiwaliks
key_dimensions: Himadri (Greater Himalayas) — average elevation ~6000m, contains main glaciers and peaks
Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) — Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat ranges; hill stations located here
Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas) — youngest, most prone to erosion, Duns/Duars located between Shiwalik and Lesser Himalayas
Dun valleys (Dehradun, Patli Dun, Kotli Dun) — longitudinal valleys between Lesser Himalayas and Shiwaliks, UPSC location trap

concepts.name: Peninsular Plateau: Deccan Trap, Central Highlands, and Eastern Plateau
key_dimensions: Deccan Trap vs. Deccan Plateau — Deccan Trap is volcanic lava formation (NW Deccan); Deccan Plateau is broader physiographic unit
Central Highlands (Malwa, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand) — north of Vindhyas, drain into Ganga vs. southward drainage trap
Chota Nagpur Plateau — junction of Jharkhand, WB, Odisha; mineral wealth; part of peninsular plateau not Deccan
Meghalaya Plateau (Shillong Plateau) — detached block of peninsular plateau, separated by Garo-Rajmahal gap

concepts.name: Western Ghats: Passes, Peaks, and Watershed Role
key_dimensions: Three main passes — Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat, Pal Ghat (Palakkad Gap) — their railway/road connectivity significance
Palakkad Gap — only major break in Western Ghats, allows moisture penetration, affects Kerala-Tamil Nadu climate
Highest peaks — Anamudi (2695m, highest in peninsular India), Doddabetta (highest in Nilgiris)
Western Ghats as water divide — rivers flowing west (short, fast) vs. east (long, slow) — asymmetry trap

concepts.name: Eastern Ghats: Discontinuous Nature, Peaks, and River Gaps
key_dimensions: Eastern Ghats are discontinuous — cut by eastward-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri)
Mahendragiri (Odisha) — highest peak of Eastern Ghats, often confused with Mahendragiri in other contexts
Eastern Ghats vs. Western Ghats — elevation, continuity, rainfall shadow comparison
Shevaroy Hills, Javadi Hills, Nallamala Hills — local names of Eastern Ghats segments, UPSC map-based traps

concepts.name: Vindhya-Satpura Range System: Orientation and Drainage Divide Role
key_dimensions: Vindhyas — east-west range, historical north-south cultural divide; not a watershed between Ganga and peninsular rivers (common misconception)
Satpura Range — fault block mountain, runs parallel to Narmada and Tapi rift valleys
Narmada-Tapi rift valleys — flow westward in grabens (rift valleys), unlike most peninsular rivers
Amarkantak — source of Narmada, Son, and Mahanadi rivers from same highland; UPSC multi-river origin trap

concepts.name: Aravalli Range: Age, Orientation, and Significance
key_dimensions: Oldest fold mountain in India (and among oldest in world) — Precambrian age, heavily eroded
NE-SW orientation — acts as partial barrier to Arabian Sea monsoon, rain shadow creates Thar Desert
Guru Shikhar (Mt. Abu, Rajasthan) — highest peak of Aravallis, only hill station in Rajasthan
Aravalli as watershed between Indus basin (Luni river) and Ganga basin rivers

concepts.name: The Indo-Gangetic Plain: Sub-divisions and Depositional Features
key_dimensions: Three sub-divisions — Bhabar (pebble-laden, rivers disappear), Terai (marshy, rivers re-emerge), Alluvial plains (Khadar and Bhangar)
Khadar vs. Bhangar — Khadar is newer flood plain alluvium (fertile), Bhangar is older upland alluvium (contains Kankar nodules)
Doab regions — land between two rivers (e.g., Ganga-Yamuna Doab); UPSC tests specific doab names
Punjab Plains vs. Ganga Plains vs. Brahmaputra Plains — differences in river behavior, deltaic nature

concepts.name: Brahmaputra Valley and Assam Plains: Physiographic Uniqueness
key_dimensions: Brahmaputra as antecedent river — older than Himalayas, cuts through them at Namcha Barwa gorge (deepest gorge in world)
Brahmaputra flows east-to-west in Tibet (Tsangpo), turns at Namcha Barwa — UPSC direction trap
Majuli Island — largest river island in world (contested), located in Brahmaputra, Assam
Assam valley between Himalayas (north) and Meghalaya Plateau (south) — unique enclosed plain structure

concepts.name: Coastal Plains of India: East vs. West Coast Comparison
key_dimensions: Western Coastal Plain — narrow, no delta formation, submerged coast (Ria coast), Khambhat and Kutch gulfs in north
Eastern Coastal Plain — wider, deltaic, emergent coast, contains major deltas (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri)
Specific named segments — Konkan, Kanara, Malabar (west); Utkal, Andhra, Coromandel (east) — location-state mapping
Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Pulicat Lake (AP/Tamil Nadu) — lagoons on eastern coast, formation by longshore drift

concepts.name: Thar Desert: Physiographic Features and Eastern Margin
key_dimensions: Eastern boundary of Thar — Aravallis (debated); Luni river drains it — only significant river, drains into Rann of Kutch
Aeolian landforms — Barchans (crescent dunes), Seifs (longitudinal dunes), Playas (ephemeral lakes/Dhands)
Rann of Kutch — seasonal salt marsh, part Great Rann and Little Rann, not a desert but often grouped physiographically
Thar as geological continuation of Sindh plains — not purely a rain-shadow desert but also due to subtropical high pressure

concepts.name: Andaman & Nicobar Islands: Physiographic and Tectonic Character
key_dimensions: Andaman & Nicobar are tips of submerged mountain range — extension of Arakan Yoma (Myanmar)
Barren Island — only active volcano in South Asia, located in Andaman Sea
Narcondam Island — dormant volcano in Andaman; UPSC often pairs it with Barren Island
Indira Point (Great Nicobar) — southernmost point of India, not Kanyakumari — classic UPSC trap

concepts.name: Lakshadweep Islands: Origin, Structure, and Comparison with A&N
key_dimensions: Coral origin (atoll type) — vs. Andaman & Nicobar (sedimentary/volcanic) — UPSC contrast trap
Located on continental shelf of India — shallow water, unlike A&N which are in deeper oceanic waters
Minicoy Island — southernmost island of Lakshadweep, geographically closer to Maldives, distinct culture
No rivers, no forests, freshwater only from groundwater and rain — physiographic constraints on habitation

concepts.name: Important River Gorges and Canyons in India
key_dimensions: Namcha Barwa gorge (Brahmaputra) — deepest river gorge in world, antecedent drainage example
Gandikota Gorge (Penna River, Andhra Pradesh) — called 'Grand Canyon of India'
Bhedaghat (Narmada) — marble rocks gorge, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh
Gorges as evidence of antecedent vs. consequent drainage — UPSC theoretical application from map features

concepts.name: Significant Plateaus: Shillong, Malwa, Chota Nagpur, Deccan — Location and Characteristics
key_dimensions: Shillong Plateau — detached part of Peninsular Plateau, separated by Rajmahal-Garo gap, receives highest rainfall due to funnel effect (Cherrapunji)
Malwa Plateau — drained by Chambal and Betwa (Ganga tributaries) in north, Narmada in south — drainage divide significance
Chota Nagpur Plateau — rich in minerals (coal, iron ore, mica), source of Damodar, Subarnarekha rivers
Deccan Plateau — tilted westward, explains why major rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow eastward to Bay of Bengal

concepts.name: Physiographic Boundary Lines and Transition Zones
key_dimensions: Rajmahal-Garo gap — separates Shillong Plateau from main Peninsular Block, Ganga flows through this gap
Narmada-Son lineament — tectonic fault line separating peninsular India from northern plains; Narmada flows along it
Bhabar-Terai transition — abrupt change in permeability from piedmont gravel to fine alluvium
McMahon Line, Line of Actual Control — physiographic correlations with Himalayan ridgelines tested in GS1 maps

concepts.name: High Altitude Lakes and Wetlands: Physiographic Formation and Location
key_dimensions: Pangong Tso — trans-boundary lake (India-China), located in Ladakh, saltwater lake, ~60% in China — UPSC boundary trap
Tsomoriri (Moriri) — high altitude Ramsar wetland in Ladakh, entirely within India unlike Pangong
Dal Lake (J&K) vs. Wular Lake — Wular is largest freshwater lake in India, tectonic origin
Loktak Lake (Manipur) — largest freshwater lake in NE India, Phumdis (floating biomass islands) — unique feature
